source.name: Acquire Data
source.description:
The Acquire Data process focuses on identifying and obtaining the data necessary to support the problem at hand, and its approach should be tailored to your specific role and needs. To maximize the value of your data investment, start by examining what data you already have access to but may not be utilizing—often, valuable information is left behind by filtering processes. Adopting a policy of ABC (Adopt, Buy, Create) encourages using existing data sources—whether internal, open-access, or purchased—before resorting to creating new data from scratch.

Additionally, it's important to remove format limitations by considering both structured and unstructured or semi-structured data sources, broadening your data acquisition mindset. Identify gaps by asking what crucial data, if accessed, could significantly improve your processes and then actively seek it out. Engaging with a diverse range of publicly available sources can also enrich your data pool, and breaking down data silos by treating data as an enterprise asset ensures broader access and better integration across your organization.
Source hierarchy context (ancestors, not additional candidates):
  BP: Business Processes - C3 Taxonomy – Business Processes
  BP-1000: Business Processes - Business processes represent a collection of related, structured activities or tasks by people or equipment in which a specific sequence produces a service or product to accomplish specific (strategic and operational) organizational goals. Efficient and streamlined execution of business processes directly contributes to the success of defence enterprises. 

A defence enterprise at its most basic level is composed of a ministry or department of defence - which is that part of the government that is responsible for matters of defence and that usually includes all branches of the military - plus the military forces - the professional organizations and units delivering the military instruments of power. This taxonomy provides a suitable framework for the defence enterprises through:
* A common language that allows comparing and linking process architectures of different organizations;
* A foundation structure for classifying processes into groups of related processes;
* A checklist or starting point for identifying candidate processes undertaken within your organization; and
* A basis for determining how process ownership can be assigned.

In the context of the C3 Taxonomy, business processes are focussed on their relevance to military missions and the achievement of superiority on the battlefield. The second layer of the associated taxonomy specifies four main categories:
* '''Govern''' -- to direct defence policy, military operations at the strategic level, as well as direct rules and standards applying to the entire defence enterprise whilst maintaining accountability for defence activity and spending.
* '''Generate''' -- to develop and create military forces, including the acquisition of the equipment, systems and other items needed so that military units are ready for operations.
* '''Operate''' -- to command and control military forces domestically and abroad, and employing the military instruments of power.
* '''Enable''' -- to allow and empower the defence enterprise to work properly by providing supporting services.
  BP-1327: Enable - The "Enable” process area includes those basic business processes that are required to run and manage any large enterprise. These generic processes focus on providing those support services that are required throughout the entire defence enterprise such as Financial Management, Human Resources Management processes, etc.. Since enabling processes are aimed at general support within the defence enterprise, they may interface as needed with almost every other process in the enterprise, be they governance, strategy, force development or operations processes. Most of the common business processes are defined in the “Enable” process area, however, those processes that are specific to the conduct of military operations are defined in the “Operate” process area (e.g. organic Tactical CIS Support, planning and providing Health Services Support (HSS) for combat operations).

The "Enable" business process area has the following breakdown:
* '''Personnel Support''' -- Describes the processes for planning, managing, and employing personnel resources to ensure effective staffing and workforce utilization.  
* '''Engineering and Infrastructure Support''' -- Contains processes that enable the organization to deliver activities without delays or impediments caused by physical environment constraints, supporting operational infrastructure.  
* '''Customer Relationship Management''' -- Maintains positive relationships with customers by identifying their needs and ensuring the service catalog supports those needs, linked closely with service level management.  
* '''CIS Support''' -- Includes processes for managing components of a Communications and Information Systems environment, supporting security, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.  
* '''Education, Training, Exercises and Evaluation''' (ETEE) -- Describes processes related to education, training, exercises, and evaluations vital for military readiness and capability development.  
* '''Analytical Support''' -- Supports decision-making outside operational contexts, providing organizational insights, data analysis, and supporting data science relations for strategic analysis.  
* '''Supplier Management''' -- Ensures value for money from suppliers, managing contracts to meet business needs and verifying supplier performance via a comprehensive supplier and contract database.  
* '''Financial Support''' -- Facilitates sound financial management across organizations through governance, resource management, internal controls, and resource efficiency, with staff compliance required.  
* '''Health Services''' -- Establishes health policies and services to support organization members’ well-being, enabling routine operational support.  
* '''Information Management''' -- Supports handling information through its lifecycle to ensure availability, quality, and appropriateness for organizational demands.  
* '''Task Management''' -- Manages the creation, assignment, tracking, and reporting of organizational tasks and their outcomes, ensuring efficient task execution.  
* '''Facility Management''' -- Ensures built environment functionality, safety, and efficiency, focusing on physical assets (Hard FM) and personnel services (Soft FM) to enhance quality of life and productivity.  
* '''Legal Support''' -- Provides legal services across all command levels, offering advice on legal implications and supporting operational planning and legal compliance.  
* Risk Management Governance -- Governs the risk management framework, overseeing its continual improvement to support risk-aware decision-making throughout the organization.
  BP-1060: Analytical Support - The processes detailed here represent the activities that are conducted to support the organization's decision making process outside of specific operational contexts. Elements of the Analytical Support processes may be implemented as components of a wider function or domain process, but except where there are analytical processes specific to certain environments, analytical functions here are described as enabling processes for the entire organization.

There is significant relationship between the Analytical Support processes and the Data Science Processes, and these have been represented independently as far as organizational structure permits.

target.name: Hydrography Services
target.description:
The Hydrography Services provide functions to access high-level and value-added information, and related computational functions required by hydrographers. The services assist hydrographers in mapping/charting the water's topographic features by measuring the depths, tides, and currents of a body of water, establishing the topography and morphology of seas, rivers, and lake beds.

  CI-1000: Community of Interest Services - The Community of Interest (COI) Services provide functions to support operations, exercises and routine activities for every single, and every possible combination of, communities of interest across all military domains and functions.

Community of Interest Services represent a collection of technical services at the back-end of communications and information systems (CIS) capabilities, focused on one or many collaborative groups of users with shared goals, interests, missions or business processes. These services are primarily meant to directly support and enable user applications and service consumption.

In the context of the C3 Taxonomy, COI services are facilitating specific military domains and functions, enabling corresponding user applications and connecting these to the core services in the back-end. The second layer of the associated taxonomy specifies two main categories:
* '''COI-Specific Services''' -- to provide functionality as required by user communities in support of operations, exercises and routine activities. These COI-specific services may have been previously referred to as "functional services" or "functional area services".
* '''COI-Enabling Services''' -- to provide COI-dependent functionality required by more than one community of interest. They are similar to core services in that they provide building blocks for domain-specific service development. The distinction between the two is that core services provide generic COI-independent capabilities for the entire enterprise (e.g. collaboration and information management services) and COI-enabling services provide those COI-dependent services that are typically shared by a group of communities (e.g. operational planning and situational awareness capabilities). A second distinction is that COI-enabling services tend to be specific for C3 processes whereas core services tend to be more generic and can be used by any business or enterprise.
  CI-1023: COI-Specific Services - The Community of Interest (COI)-Specific Services provide functions to support operations, exercises and routine activities required by specific user communities. These services may have been previously referred to as "functional services" or "functional area services".

source.name: Recognized Environmental Pictures
source.description:
The Recognized Environmental Pictures (REP) constitute information streams that convey operational, procedural and/or functional facts about the assessed situation in the functional area of environmental support, as far as relevant for the planning and conduct of operations, in a format that is suitable for electronic dissemination and for integration in electronic displays.

An REP is commonly an electronically produced compilation of information to provide geographical, hydrographical, meteorological, oceanographic and space weather data. Separate recognized pictures exist for each of these five areas of environmental support to operations.
Source hierarchy context (ancestors, not additional candidates):
  IP: Information Products - C3 Taxonomy – Information Products
  IP-1000: Information Products - Information products represent a compilation of related, structured information that can be regarded as the formal output of a business process and/or can be used as an input to other business processes. These information products can be seen as any communication or representation of knowledge such as facts, data, or opinions in any medium or form. Their definition is linked with activities in related business processes and with automation needs (applications and their respective functions).

Information products have the capacity to be delivered in any medium or form, including (structured or non-structured) textual, numerical, graphic, cartographic, narrative, or audio-visual forms. They may be uniformly consumed by more than one actor or role in more than one business process.

In the context of the C3 Taxonomy, information products are focussed on their relevance to deliver clear, complete and effective information exchange in support of military missions. The second layer of the associated taxonomy specifies six main categories:
* '''Governance Information Products''' -- about the overall system of decision-making, authority, and organizational structure, providing the core doctrine for planning, executing, and supporting operations.
* '''Domain-Specific Information Products''' -- about facts and activities pertinent to a specific military domain, existing only when no similar products are available in other domains.
* '''Operation Enabling Information Products''' -- about process activities that directly support operational outputs, such as targeting, environment preparation, force protection, and coordination, developed by various communities of interest.
* '''Operation Support Information Products''' -- about facts on activities and resources, necessary to sustain and enhance ongoing operational effectiveness of the force or organization.
* '''Situational Awareness Information Products''' -- about critical information that enables decision-makers to perceive, comprehend, and project environmental elements to conduct safe and effective missions.
* '''Management Information Products''' -- about information related to the planning, organization, and control of resources, processes, and personnel to achieve specific organizational objectives.
  IP-1005: Situational Awareness Information Products - The Situational Awareness (SA) Information Products convey facts about the critical information to decision-makers in complex, dynamic areas such as military command and control. Situation Awareness is the perception of environmental elements with respect to time and/or space, the comprehension of their meaning, and the projection of their status, affecting the safe, expedient and effective conduct of the mission. It involves being aware of what is happening in the vicinity to understand how information, events, and actions (both own and others) might impact goals and objectives, both immediately and in the near future.
  IP-1102: Recognized Pictures - The Recognized Pictures (RPs) constitute information streams that contain facts about the critical geospatial information from specific operation domains and/or functions in the context of a mission or exercise, and in the scope of an area of operations or a corresponding environment. The fact that the information is geospatially enhanced implies that it can be displayed on maps and correlated with compatible geospatial data from any compatible recognized picture.

Data for recognized pictures are received from national, theatre, and/or tactical sensor feeds and processed in services designed for the collection, fusion and management of this data and managed by a force or organization's coordination centre.

These Recognized Pictures can be integrated in a single data feed and/or a single display of a common operational picture (COP), which includes the ability to complement these pictures with functional enhancements with an aim toward enhancing situational awareness (SA). The COP is a product and not a system. It can be displayed and managed on command and control information systems (C2IS) comprised of the necessary applications to process, manage and display required data and information. As such, on C2IS the COP may include additional information (e.g. commander’s intent, battle plans, projection overlays).

target.description:

source.name: Acquire Data
source.description:
The Acquire Data process focuses on identifying and obtaining the data necessary to support the problem at hand, and its approach should be tailored to your specific role and needs. To maximize the value of your data investment, start by examining what data you already have access to but may not be utilizing—often, valuable information is left behind by filtering processes. Adopting a policy of ABC (Adopt, Buy, Create) encourages using existing data sources—whether internal, open-access, or purchased—before resorting to creating new data from scratch.

Additionally, it's important to remove format limitations by considering both structured and unstructured or semi-structured data sources, broadening your data acquisition mindset. Identify gaps by asking what crucial data, if accessed, could significantly improve your processes and then actively seek it out. Engaging with a diverse range of publicly available sources can also enrich your data pool, and breaking down data silos by treating data as an enterprise asset ensures broader access and better integration across your organization.

  BP: Business Processes - C3 Taxonomy – Business Processes
  BP-1000: Business Processes - Business processes represent a collection of related, structured activities or tasks by people or equipment in which a specific sequence produces a service or product to accomplish specific (strategic and operational) organizational goals. Efficient and streamlined execution of business processes directly contributes to the success of defence enterprises. 

A defence enterprise at its most basic level is composed of a ministry or department of defence - which is that part of the government that is responsible for matters of defence and that usually includes all branches of the military - plus the military forces - the professional organizations and units delivering the military instruments of power. This taxonomy provides a suitable framework for the defence enterprises through:
* A common language that allows comparing and linking process architectures of different organizations;
* A foundation structure for classifying processes into groups of related processes;
* A checklist or starting point for identifying candidate processes undertaken within your organization; and
* A basis for determining how process ownership can be assigned.

In the context of the C3 Taxonomy, business processes are focussed on their relevance to military missions and the achievement of superiority on the battlefield. The second layer of the associated taxonomy specifies four main categories:
* '''Govern''' -- to direct defence policy, military operations at the strategic level, as well as direct rules and standards applying to the entire defence enterprise whilst maintaining accountability for defence activity and spending.
* '''Generate''' -- to develop and create military forces, including the acquisition of the equipment, systems and other items needed so that military units are ready for operations.
* '''Operate''' -- to command and control military forces domestically and abroad, and employing the military instruments of power.
* '''Enable''' -- to allow and empower the defence enterprise to work properly by providing supporting services.
  BP-1327: Enable - The "Enable” process area includes those basic business processes that are required to run and manage any large enterprise. These generic processes focus on providing those support services that are required throughout the entire defence enterprise such as Financial Management, Human Resources Management processes, etc.. Since enabling processes are aimed at general support within the defence enterprise, they may interface as needed with almost every other process in the enterprise, be they governance, strategy, force development or operations processes. Most of the common business processes are defined in the “Enable” process area, however, those processes that are specific to the conduct of military operations are defined in the “Operate” process area (e.g. organic Tactical CIS Support, planning and providing Health Services Support (HSS) for combat operations).

The "Enable" business process area has the following breakdown:
* '''Personnel Support''' -- Describes the processes for planning, managing, and employing personnel resources to ensure effective staffing and workforce utilization.  
* '''Engineering and Infrastructure Support''' -- Contains processes that enable the organization to deliver activities without delays or impediments caused by physical environment constraints, supporting operational infrastructure.  
* '''Customer Relationship Management''' -- Maintains positive relationships with customers by identifying their needs and ensuring the service catalog supports those needs, linked closely with service level management.  
* '''CIS Support''' -- Includes processes for managing components of a Communications and Information Systems environment, supporting security, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.  
* '''Education, Training, Exercises and Evaluation''' (ETEE) -- Describes processes related to education, training, exercises, and evaluations vital for military readiness and capability development.  
* '''Analytical Support''' -- Supports decision-making outside operational contexts, providing organizational insights, data analysis, and supporting data science relations for strategic analysis.  
* '''Supplier Management''' -- Ensures value for money from suppliers, managing contracts to meet business needs and verifying supplier performance via a comprehensive supplier and contract database.  
* '''Financial Support''' -- Facilitates sound financial management across organizations through governance, resource management, internal controls, and resource efficiency, with staff compliance required.  
* '''Health Services''' -- Establishes health policies and services to support organization members’ well-being, enabling routine operational support.  
* '''Information Management''' -- Supports handling information through its lifecycle to ensure availability, quality, and appropriateness for organizational demands.  
* '''Task Management''' -- Manages the creation, assignment, tracking, and reporting of organizational tasks and their outcomes, ensuring efficient task execution.  
* '''Facility Management''' -- Ensures built environment functionality, safety, and efficiency, focusing on physical assets (Hard FM) and personnel services (Soft FM) to enhance quality of life and productivity.  
* '''Legal Support''' -- Provides legal services across all command levels, offering advice on legal implications and supporting operational planning and legal compliance.  
* Risk Management Governance -- Governs the risk management framework, overseeing its continual improvement to support risk-aware decision-making throughout the organization.
  BP-1060: Analytical Support - The processes detailed here represent the activities that are conducted to support the organization's decision making process outside of specific operational contexts. Elements of the Analytical Support processes may be implemented as components of a wider function or domain process, but except where there are analytical processes specific to certain environments, analytical functions here are described as enabling processes for the entire organization.

There is significant relationship between the Analytical Support processes and the Data Science Processes, and these have been represented independently as far as organizational structure permits.

The Recognized Environmental Pictures (REP) constitute information streams that convey operational, procedural and/or functional facts about the assessed situation in the functional area of environmental support, as far as relevant for the planning and conduct of operations, in a format that is suitable for electronic dissemination and for integration in electronic displays.

Their definition is linked with activities in related business processes and with automation needs (applications and their respective functions).

* '''Governance Information Products''' -- about the overall system of decision-making, authority, and organizational structure, providing the core doctrine for planning, executing, and supporting operations.
* '''Domain-Specific Information Products''' -- about facts and activities pertinent to a specific military domain, existing only when no similar products are available in other domains.
* '''Operation Enabling Information Products''' -- about process activities that directly support operational outputs, such as targeting, environment preparation, force protection, and coordination, developed by various communities of interest.
* '''Operation Support Information Products''' -- about facts on activities and resources, necessary to sustain and enhance ongoing operational effectiveness of the force or organization.
* '''Situational Awareness Information Products''' -- about critical information that enables decision-makers to perceive, comprehend, and project environmental elements to conduct safe and effective missions.

source.name: Recognized Environmental Pictures
source.description:
The Recognized Environmental Pictures (REP) constitute information streams that convey operational, procedural and/or functional facts about the assessed situation in the functional area of environmental support, as far as relevant for the planning and conduct of operations, in a format that is suitable for electronic dissemination and for integration in electronic displays.

An REP is commonly an electronically produced compilation of information to provide geographical, hydrographical, meteorological, oceanographic and space weather data. Separate recognized pictures exist for each of these five areas of environmental support to operations.
Source hierarchy context (ancestors, not additional candidates):
  IP: Information Products - C3 Taxonomy – Information Products
  IP-1000: Information Products - Information products represent a compilation of related, structured information that can be regarded as the formal output of a business process and/or can be used as an input to other business processes. These information products can be seen as any communication or representation of knowledge such as facts, data, or opinions in any medium or form. Their definition is linked with activities in related business processes and with automation needs (applications and their respective functions).

Information products have the capacity to be delivered in any medium or form, including (structured or non-structured) textual, numerical, graphic, cartographic, narrative, or audio-visual forms. They may be uniformly consumed by more than one actor or role in more than one business process.

In the context of the C3 Taxonomy, information products are focussed on their relevance to deliver clear, complete and effective information exchange in support of military missions. The second layer of the associated taxonomy specifies six main categories:
* '''Governance Information Products''' -- about the overall system of decision-making, authority, and organizational structure, providing the core doctrine for planning, executing, and supporting operations.
* '''Domain-Specific Information Products''' -- about facts and activities pertinent to a specific military domain, existing only when no similar products are available in other domains.
* '''Operation Enabling Information Products''' -- about process activities that directly support operational outputs, such as targeting, environment preparation, force protection, and coordination, developed by various communities of interest.
* '''Operation Support Information Products''' -- about facts on activities and resources, necessary to sustain and enhance ongoing operational effectiveness of the force or organization.
* '''Situational Awareness Information Products''' -- about critical information that enables decision-makers to perceive, comprehend, and project environmental elements to conduct safe and effective missions.
* '''Management Information Products''' -- about information related to the planning, organization, and control of resources, processes, and personnel to achieve specific organizational objectives.
  IP-1005: Situational Awareness Information Products - The Situational Awareness (SA) Information Products convey facts about the critical information to decision-makers in complex, dynamic areas such as military command and control. Situation Awareness is the perception of environmental elements with respect to time and/or space, the comprehension of their meaning, and the projection of their status, affecting the safe, expedient and effective conduct of the mission. It involves being aware of what is happening in the vicinity to understand how information, events, and actions (both own and others) might impact goals and objectives, both immediately and in the near future.
  IP-1102: Recognized Pictures - The Recognized Pictures (RPs) constitute information streams that contain facts about the critical geospatial information from specific operation domains and/or functions in the context of a mission or exercise, and in the scope of an area of operations or a corresponding environment. The fact that the information is geospatially enhanced implies that it can be displayed on maps and correlated with compatible geospatial data from any compatible recognized picture.

Data for recognized pictures are received from national, theatre, and/or tactical sensor feeds and processed in services designed for the collection, fusion and management of this data and managed by a force or organization's coordination centre.

These Recognized Pictures can be integrated in a single data feed and/or a single display of a common operational picture (COP), which includes the ability to complement these pictures with functional enhancements with an aim toward enhancing situational awareness (SA). The COP is a product and not a system. It can be displayed and managed on command and control information systems (C2IS) comprised of the necessary applications to process, manage and display required data and information. As such, on C2IS the COP may include additional information (e.g. commander’s intent, battle plans, projection overlays).
